note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Difficulty swallowing for several weeks with chest pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male presenting with dysphagia and chest pain on swallowing that has been occurring over the last several weeks. He reports that pain occurs most of the time when swallowing, particularly with larger pieces of food that feel like they are getting stuck. He denies weight loss and reports recent weight gain of approximately 10 pounds over the last month. He attributes increased stress to a recent move from the west coast to the east coast over the last couple of months, during which he has been eating less healthy foods including pizza and burgers, and drinking more. He denies hemoptysis, hematochezia, or melena. He reports occasional epigastric pain but denies nausea or vomiting.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies fever, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Reports occasional epigastric pain. Denies blood in stool or dark tarry stools. All other systems reviewed and negative.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
None documented.

MEDICATIONS
None documented at time of visit.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is currently relocating from west coast to east coast. Reports increased stress related to move and concern about traveling with pet dog. Reports recent increase in consumption of fast food (pizza, burgers) and alcohol due to stress of relocation. Denies tobacco use.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: BP 133/70, HR normal, Temp afebrile, RR 19, O2 sat 100% on room air. 
General: Weight gain of 10 pounds noted over last month.
HEENT: No ulcers or thrush noted. Tonsils midline.
Neck: No adenopathy. No thyromegaly.
Abdomen: Nondistended with active bowel sounds. Epigastric palpation elicits pain. Negative Murphy's sign. No peritoneal signs or rebound tenderness.
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Skin: No rash, lesions, or bruising.
Eyes: Equal and reactive to light bilaterally.

RESULTS
Barium swallow: Two areas of mild narrowing in the mid and lower portions of the esophagus consistent with esophagitis.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Acute esophagitis with dysphagia and chest pain on swallowing.

Plan:
1. Prescribe Protonix 40 mg once daily, take first thing in the morning.
2. Prescribe Carafate 1 gram four times daily for one month to coat esophageal and gastric lining.
3. Schedule upper endoscopy to rule out other pathology.
4. Dietary modifications: decrease alcohol and caffeine, avoid citrus fruits and spicy foods until symptoms improve. Eat slowly and chew food thoroughly.
5. Follow-up visit next week for endoscopy.
